newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar sees potential for spot LNG sales to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Qatar sees potential for spot LNG sales to Europe.

text.p: Gulf Arab Qatar could export tankers of its liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Europe despite the high cost of such long-haul sales and competition from other suppliers, a senior Qatari energy official said on Sunday.

"We foresee windows of opportunities, even with the present challenges, of getting some Qatar LNG to Europe by possible spot spot sales through optimisation of current capacities of LNG projects or excess capacities," Nasser Jaidah, a director at state-woned Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC)said.

The long-haul high cost of transporting LNG from the Gulf to Europe and competitive alternative supplies from Russia, Norway amd Algeria have led most analysts to argue that exports of new sources of Gulf LNG to Europe will be limited and uneconomic.
Qatar, like Oman, Abu Dhabi and Iran, has earmarked power utilities in Japan, South Korea, southeast Asia and India as the main long-term market for its liquefied gas exports.

"Qatar is willing to play its role and alleviate the challenges facing gas supplies to Europe...European countries should reciprocate...by guaranteeing a reasonable pricing mechanism," Jaidah, QGPC director for exploration, development and new ventures said.
The Gulf state is planning three multi-billion LNG projects and exports from its first project -- Qatargas -- are scheduled to begin in December to Japan.
Abu Dhabi, the Gulf's main LNG seller, currently has limited term sales with Spain, France and Belgium though the vast majority of its LNG exports are sold to Japan.
Jaidah was speaking at a two-day gas conference organised by the six-member Gulf Cooperation Council and the European Commission to examine Europe's growing gas demand.
